issues.problem: Regression in 86504f4: fabrications that were caught at dd40805 are now 'supported'. (1) 'with no X' is rewritten to 'without X' only for the polarity test, while _quantifier_conflict runs WITHOUT_RE on the un-normalised clause, so 'with no X' is neither a negation nor a term and a claim asserting X matches. (2) NEGATION_IDIOM_RE deletes 'no more than' / 'no less than' / 'no fewer than' / 'nothing less than', so the quote reads as the bare comparative and 'more than 50' is supported by 'no more than 50'. quality-gates.md says 'with no X' and 'without X' are compared as terms (zero/without against a plain assertion is 'contradicted').
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a5-probe/bin/score5b.py at HEAD: 'Acme offers SCIM' vs 'Acme offers SSO with no SCIM' supported; 'Acme charges a setup fee' vs '... on all plans with no setup fee' supported; 'Acme has an offline mode' vs 'Acme ships with no offline mode' supported; 'Acme's migration caused downtime' vs '... with no downtime' supported; 'Acme has more than 50 customers' vs 'Acme has no more than 50 customers' supported; 'less than 99%' vs 'nothing less than 99%' supported; control 'without SCIM' -> contradicted. All 'partial' at dd40805. End to end (bin/e2e.sh, SKILL.md command, --strict), runs/fab7.tsv rows 1-3: HEAD supported (run exit 0), dd40805 partial (exit 1).
issues.suggested_fix: Run the quantifier check on _normalize_negation(clause) (or include 'with no' in WITHOUT_RE), and treat 'no X' after a verb the same way. Strip a comparative idiom only when the claim does not carry the bare comparative; when the claim says 'more/less/fewer than N' and the quote 'no more/less/fewer than N', return contradicted (or needs_review). Add these pairs to the fabrication corpus.

issues.problem: Honest comparison claims are 'contradicted' (criterion b), one of them against an identical quote. ENTITY_LIST_RE reads 'SCIM and Initech' / 'SSO and SCIM, and Initech' as a coordinated list although 'Initech' opens a new clause, so _variants builds nonsense clauses ('Acme supports SCIM does not', 'Acme offers SSO offers neither') whose polarity conflicts with the quote. The note is misleading ('polarity: the source says "Acme supports SCIM"', i.e. the source agrees). These are the 'A supports X and B does not' sentences solution-landscape reports are made of; the r4 fix covered the shape only on the quote side.
issues.evidence: End to end, REVF-H8a5-probe/runs/hon9.tsv through bin/e2e.sh: HEAD status fail, exit 1, 3 contradicted + 1 needs_review: 'Acme supports SCIM and Initech does not' vs 'Acme supports SCIM; Initech does not' (contradicted); 'Acme offers SSO and Initech lacks it' vs '..., while Initech lacks it' (contradicted); 'Okta supports SAML and OneLogin does not' vs 'Okta supports SAML. OneLogin does not.' (contradicted); the identical pair 'Acme supports SCIM and Initech does not' (needs_review). dd40805: 3 partial + 1 supported. bin/honest5.py: 'Acme offers SSO and SCIM, and Initech offers neither' vs the identical sentence -> contradicted (supported at dd40805; also e2e runs/fab9.tsv row 7); 'Slack integrates with Jira and Asana does not' vs '...; Asana does not' contradicted; 'Acme supports Kubernetes and Initech does not' vs '..., and Initech does not' needs_review (supported at dd40805). With 'SCIM provisioning' (lowercase word before 'and') the same pairs are supported (runs/e-hon8.out), which isolates the list regex.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not build list variants when the last item is followed by a predicate (an auxiliary, a verb, 'does not', 'lacks', 'offers neither'): split the clause at 'and <Name> <verb>' first. Skip variants when the squashed claim clause equals a quote clause. Add these comparison claims, verbatim and with ';' / '.' / ', while' quotes, to the honest corpus.

issues.problem: Role swaps are still 'supported' unless the voices differ or both gaps are at most three words without a preposition. quality-gates.md now promises 'the same named things ... in another order or voice ... roles cannot be settled by words, so needs_review' and removed role swaps from the limits, and the fix report lists 'role swap/voice ambiguity' as fixed. A passive-passive swap has 'by' in the gap, and copula/preposition relations (owned by, subsidiary of, cheaper than, invested in, licenses to, spun off from, migrated from X to Y) all have prepositions.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a5-probe/bin/roles5.py at HEAD, 10/14 supported: 'Acme was acquired by Initech' vs 'Initech was acquired by Acme'; 'Acme is a subsidiary of Initech' vs the reverse; 'Acme is owned by Initech'; 'Acme is cheaper than Initech'; 'Acme is faster than Initech on the TPC-H benchmark'; 'Microsoft invested $10 billion in OpenAI' vs 'OpenAI invested $10 billion in Microsoft'; 'Acme licenses its technology to Initech'; 'Acme sold its stake in Initech in 2022'; 'Acme spun off from Initech in 2019'; 'Acme migrated from Postgres to MySQL' vs 'from MySQL to Postgres'. End to end runs/fab9.tsv rows 4-6 supported. Only short active gaps (sued, pays, beat, replaced X with Y) give needs_review.
issues.suggested_fix: Conservative rule: when two or more claim entities occur in one aligned quote clause in a different order, return needs_review whatever the gap (or treat by/of/than/to/in/from gaps as role-bearing). Add the roles5 pairs to the fabrication corpus; keep the honest active/passive paraphrases as needs_review.

issues.problem: Fabrication classes outside the documented limits (antonyms outside the table, unit synonyms, idioms restating a negation, world knowledge) still pass the strict gate as 'supported', contrary to 'supported only when its words, figures and names unambiguously match a quoted source span': (a) a figure or year that the quote attaches to another entity (entities are dropped from the figure's stems and checked anywhere in the quote); (b) names and predicates taken from different clauses or sentences of one quote; (c) ranges that open with 'one' ('one to three days', 'one or two') are not ranges, so the upper end alone matches - the r4 range bug class, and test_ranges_are_ranges pins n('one or two') == 'one or 2'; (d) period swaps: a quarter (Q2/Q3 are entities, not bound to the figure), 'per month' vs 'per year' (filler), a year in parentheses; (e) modality and a missed cue: 'plans to', 'will', 'is expected to', 'is considering', 'only if', a question, and 'failed to' (NEGATION_RE has 'fails? to' only).

End to end (bin/e2e.sh, --strict): runs/fab8.tsv exit 0, both supported; runs/fab7.tsv rows 5-10 and runs/fab9.tsv rows 1-3 supported. All of these were also supported at dd40805 (pre-existing), and none is in the documented limits.
issues.suggested_fix: Under 'conservative + escalate', escalate instead of supporting: (a) when the quote segment holding a matched figure or year names a different entity and not the claim's subject, needs_review; (b) require the claim's entities and its key terms to co-occur in one quote clause (or sentence) for 'supported'; (c) let a lone 'one' start a range when 'to'/'or'/'-' and a number follow, and fix the pinned test; (d) bind Q1-Q4/H1/FY periods like years, keep 'per <period>' as part of the unit, split segments at parentheses; (e) add 'failed to', 'refused to' and modal/future cues (plans to, will, expected to, aims to, considering, '?', 'only if') as needs_review triggers. Anything left out must be listed in quality-gates.md's limits.

issues.problem: A sentence that starts with a digit (or a lowercase brand) is never split from the one before it, even across a paragraph break, because SENTENCE_RE requires an upper-case letter next. An uncited '62% of ...' paragraph is merged into the previous cited sentence and inherits its citation. With the three-valued gate it is then 'needs_review' (strict passes) instead of 'unsupported' (strict fails), which contradicts SKILL.md ('--strict exits 1 ... on any unsupported or uncited factual claim'). Pre-existing splitter; this round turned the outcome from a failure into a listed review item.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a5-probe/runs/e-merge: report 'Acme has 500 employees in Berlin [1].\n\n62% of Fortune 500 companies use Acme in production.' -> 1 claim (both paragraphs), needs_review, status pass, exit 0. Same report with 'Sixty-two percent of ...' (runs/e-merge2) -> 2 claims, the second unsupported, status fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Split at a blank line unconditionally and let SENTENCE_RE also split before a digit or a lower-case letter after '. ' when a paragraph break or a citation marker precedes it.
